item.title: Canton Ticino, tunnel fire on board a train: but it's a drill
item.description: Rescue exercise in the Monte Ceneri tunnel with 50 extras and 100 rescuers.
item.content:encoded:
## In short - Rescue exercise in the Monte Ceneri tunnel - Participants: 50 extras, 100 rescuers - Simulated fire on board a train
## Key facts - **What**: Rescue exercise - When: Night between Saturday 5 and Sunday 6 September - Where: Monte Ceneri base tunnel - Who: SBB, Cantonal Police, Ticino intervention forces - Amount: Not specified
Last night, SBB, the cantonal police, and Ticino intervention forces conducted a rescue exercise in the Monte Ceneri base tunnel. The event's objective was to verify and optimize the alert system, evacuation and recovery processes, and collaboration among the forces involved. Everything went smoothly, achieving a fully satisfactory result that contributes to increasing the safety of travelers and staff.
Around fifty extras and a hundred rescuers were engaged from just before midnight on Saturday 5 to five in the morning on Sunday 6 September, during a planned maintenance window – limiting customer inconvenience but ensuring a realistic scenario. A fire caused by a technical malfunction in the driver's cab of a Giruno train traveling through the Monte Ceneri base tunnel was simulated. The flames quickly gain strength without being noticed, and the emergency brake is activated. Due to the fire, dense smoke, and sudden braking, injuries to some people are simulated.
Test on one of the worst possible scenarios In Switzerland, rail traffic is very safe, and it is highly unlikely that an event like the one simulated in this exercise will occur. However, thanks to this scenario, the coordinated alert system was positively tested, starting from the train personnel, through the SBB south control center in Pollegio, to the cantonal intervention force directions. Evacuation and first aid procedures were also positively tested. Areas where procedures can be made more efficient were identified, and after a more in-depth analysis, if necessary, these processes will be adapted. ### Implications for Cross-Border Workers The rescue exercise in the Monte Ceneri tunnel has important implications for cross-border workers who use the train daily to travel between Italy and Switzerland. The simulation of a fire on board a train is an extreme event, but preparation and collaboration between emergency services are crucial to ensure the safety of all passengers, including cross-border workers. The coordinated alert and evacuation procedures tested during the exercise contribute to improving the overall safety of the railway system, making travel safer for everyone.
### Evacuation Procedures During the exercise, evacuation and first aid procedures were tested. A fire on board a train was simulated, with flames quickly gaining strength and the emergency brake suddenly activating. This scenario allowed the effectiveness of evacuation and first aid procedures to be assessed, identifying areas for improvement to make the procedures more efficient. After a more in-depth analysis, if necessary, these processes will be adapted to ensure maximum possible safety.
### Collaboration between Emergency Services Collaboration between emergency services was a key element of the exercise. The coordinated alert, starting from the train personnel to the directions of the cantonal emergency services, allowed the effectiveness of communication and collaboration between the different entities involved to be tested. This type of exercise is fundamental to ensure that, in the event of a real emergency, all emergency services are ready to respond quickly and effectively.

It is important that cross-border commuters are aware of evacuation procedures and first aid, and that they always follow the instructions of the on-board personnel in case of an emergency. The safety of passengers is a priority for the SBB and the intervention forces, and this type of exercise contributes to ensuring that all passengers, including cross-border commuters, are protected.

item.title: Garzeno border: cost and tax guide 2024
item.description: From 2024, the deductible for new frontier workers is €10,000. How to live in Garzeno and work in Ticino: tax at source, G permit, AVS, LAMal and practical procedures.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - The New Frontier Agreement comes into force from 1 January 2024 with new tax rules. - New frontier workers: deductible €10,000, old frontier workers: exemption €7,500 until 2033. - Tax at source withheld ONLY in Switzerland, never in both countries. - Permit G allows you to live in Italy and work legally in Ticino.
## Key facts - **What**: New Frontier Agreement between Italy and Switzerland on taxation and social rights - When: Signed 23 December 2020, ratified Italy (Law 83, 13 June 2023), effective from 1 January 2024 - Where: Frontalieri province Como (Garzeno) towards Canton Ticino - Who: New frontier workers (after 17 July 2023) and old frontier workers (with transitional regime 2024-2033) - Excess: €10,000 per year (new), €7,500 (old) exempt from tax - Tax: Withheld from Switzerland, recoverable in Italy through declaration 730 (EC framework) - Permit: Document G for Italian residence and Swiss work
From 1 January 2024, the New Frontier Agreement between Italy and Switzerland has redesigned the tax rules for those who live in Garzeno and work in Ticino. The agreement, signed on 23 December 2020 and ratified in Italy with Law 83 of 13 June 2023, introduces a crucial new feature: the €10,000 deductible for new frontier workers. Those who were already border workers before 17 July 2023 benefit instead from a transitional regime with an exemption of €7,500 from 2024 to 2033.
A fundamental aspect for those who reside in ### How does taxation change from 2024
The introduction of a €10,000 allowance for new cross-border commuters means that the first €10,000 of your gross salary (summed on an annual basis) is not subject to any taxation in Switzerland or Italy. Everything you earn above this threshold is subject to the ordinary withholding tax regime administered by the AFC (Federal Tax Administration) and the cantonal tax authorities of Ticino.
Consider a hypothetical scenario: a cross-border commuter living in Garzeno and earning €50,000 gross annually has a taxable base of €40,000 (50,000 minus 10,000 allowance). The Swiss withholding tax is applied to these €40,000, which varies depending on the canton of Ticino and personal circumstances (marital status, number of children, mortgage expenses, etc.). The withholding tax rate is not fixed; it depends on individual parameters and is recalculated each year by the employer or notified by the cantonal tax office. The cross-border commuter receives a certificate with the total amount paid (the withholding tax certificate), which is then declared in the Italian model 730 to obtain the tax credit and possible refund.
For old cross-border commuters (those who were already cross-border commuters before July 17, 2023), the situation changes: they benefit from a €7,500 allowance until December 31, 2033, after which they will switch to the standard regime for new cross-border commuters (€10,000).
### Health insurance, AVS, and LPP: social rights
An often overlooked aspect is health insurance. Cross-border commuters have the right to choose between Swiss health insurance (LAMal) and Italian health insurance (SSN system, with coverage in Switzerland through the EHIC card). Those living in Garzeno and working in Ticino can opt for LAMal, which provides coverage in Switzerland with adult deductibles ranging from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500 annually, depending on the chosen policy.
In addition to LAMal, the cross-border commuter contributes to the AVS/AI system (Swiss social security) with a rate of 5.3% on the salary as an employee, plus an employer contribution. These contributions count towards the Swiss pension (first pillar). If the employer is affiliated with an LPP fund (second pillar), the cross-border commuter also contributes to this with rates ranging from 7 to 18% depending on the age group (from 25 years). In addition to the mandatory contributions, the cross-border commuter can subscribe to additional pension forms (third pillar 3a). These deadlines, percentages, and administration are managed by the AFC at the federal level and the cantonal tax authorities of Ticino. For specifics on calculating your position, you can consult the [salary calculator](nav:calculator) that integrates the 2024 scenarios.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Step-by-step procedure: how to start as a commuter Garzeno-Ticino
If you are considering moving your residence to Garzeno while keeping a job in Ticino, here are the concrete steps:
1. Sign a work contract with a Ticino company. The employer must be willing to sponsor your G Permit application with the SEM (State Secretariat for Migration). Verify the contract especially for tax aspects: where the withholding tax is calculated (usually by the employer or the Ticino cantonal tax office), and if the AVS/AI/IPG (5.3% employee) and LAINF (0.7-1.5%) contributions are deducted.
2. Apply for the G Permit at the Ticino cantonal immigration office. You will need: a valid passport, an original signed work contract, proof of residence in Garzeno (utility bills, lease, registry office registration), and a certificate of no criminal record. The process takes an average of 1-3 months.
3. Register with the Garzeno municipality as an Italian resident and notify the Italian Revenue Agency of the change of residence. This is necessary to correctly receive the 730 form and the CUD (Unique Employee Certificate) from the Swiss employer.
**4. Choose health insurance.** If you opt for the Swiss LAMal, sign up with a recognized insurer in Ticino (e.g., CSS, Helsana, Groupe Mutuel). If you prefer the Italian SSN system with cross-border coverage (EHIC), notify your employer. For details on LAMal, consult our [health insurance comparator](nav:health).
5. Verify with the AFC or the Ticino cantonal tax office how the withholding tax is calculated on your pay slip. Request an information sheet (usually free) with the federal, cantonal, and municipal rates that will apply to your situation (marital status, number of children, expenses).
### Practical Tools and Resources
To calculate your net monthly income (gross minus withholding tax, AVS/LPP contributions, insurance) in advance, you can use the [salary calculator](nav:calculator) of Frontaliere Ticino, which integrates the 2024 rates of the New Agreement and Swiss social contributions according to AFC regulations.
Another useful resource is to consult the official AFC website (afc.admin.ch) to download the brochure on Italian commuters in Switzerland, or contact the Ticino cantonal tax office (administrative headquarters in Bellinzona) for specific situations. A tax advisor is not necessary for simple employment cases, but it is recommended for self-employment income or complex investments.
Finally, if you are considering a permanent move to Garzeno, use the [cost of living comparator](nav:cost-of-living) Ticino-Italy to understand how much more or less you will spend on housing, food, transportation, and services compared to the area where you work in Ticino. Also consider commuting costs (fuel, vehicle wear, insurance, parking, tolls) in your monthly budget. For in-depth information on pension aspects and coordination between the Swiss and Italian systems, consult our [pension calculator](nav:pension).

item.title: Living in Sumirago, working in Ticino: border guide
item.description: Practical guide to living in Sumirago and working in Ticino: permits, border taxation, administrative procedures and what to consider before transferring.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Cross-border workers from Sumirago to Ticino: tax rules, G permits, and new agreement from 2024 - Withholding tax deducted in Switzerland, tax credit in Italy via CE form - Annual exemption €10,000 for new cross-border workers (from 17/7/2023); €7,500 for old cross-border workers until 2033 - AVS contributions 5.3% deducted from employee + multi-pillar management (LPP from 7-18%)
## Key facts - **Who**: Cross-border workers residing in Italy and working in Canton Ticino - What: Living in Sumirago (Varese province) and working in Ticino - Permits: G permit (cross-border residence) - Taxation: Withholding tax in Switzerland + tax credit in Italy (CE form) - Current agreement: New Cross-border Workers Agreement from January 1, 2024 - Exemption: €10,000 annually for new cross-border workers - Contributions: AVS/AI/IPG 5.3% employee; LPP 7–18% for age bracket (from 25 years); LAINF 0.7–1.5%
Living in Sumirago, a municipality in the province of Varese, and commuting daily to Ticino for work is a real scenario for cross-border workers seeking a balance between housing costs and job opportunities in Switzerland. The province of Varese, thanks to its border location, represents a residential alternative for those working in Canton Ticino.
What sets this choice apart is the complex tax and administrative regulations governing cross-border work between Italy and Switzerland. In recent years, the regulatory frameworks have been significantly adjusted to meet the changing needs of geographical mobility and the labor market.
### The new regulatory framework from 2024
With the entry into force of the New Cross-border Workers Agreement on January 1, 2024, the tax situation for cross-border workers has undergone a structural change. The agreement, signed on December 23, 2020, and ratified by Italy with Law 83 of June 13, 2023, introduces a tax regime that affects all those who start working as cross-border workers after July 17, 2023.
For new cross-border workers, an annual exemption of €10,000 on employment income has been established. This measure represents a significant change from the previous regime. Those who were already cross-border workers before July 17, 2023 (so-called "old cross-border workers") continue to benefit from an exemption of €7,500 during a transitional regime that will remain in force until 2033.
Cross-border taxation follows a precise system: the withholding tax is deducted in Switzerland at the time of salary payment. Italy, in turn, avoids double taxation through the recognition of a tax credit, using the CE form of the income tax return (model 730). This system is governed by the Convention against Double Taxation between Italy and Switzerland, signed on December 9, 1976.
A cross-border worker residing in Sumirago and working in Ticino is subject to federal, cantonal, and municipal Swiss tax rates according to the administrative structure of the workplace. At the same time, they declare their income in Italy according to their tax residence in Sumirago. The administrative management of taxation is entrusted, at the federal Swiss level, to the Federal Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV), while in Ticino the cantonal tax administration intervenes. On the Italian side, the Revenue Agency coordinates the recovery of the declaration and tax.
To understand how this taxation affects your net income based on your gross salary, you can consult the [paycheck calculator](nav:calculator) that simulates the impact of deductions. ## Administrative and Contributory Planning
Choosing to live in Sumirago to work in Ticino requires understanding not only the tax aspect but also the mandatory social contributions in Switzerland and the management of documentation between the two States.
### AVS/AI Contributions and Multi-Pillar Pension System
As an employed cross-border worker in Ticino, you will automatically be enrolled in the Swiss social security system. The weekly deduction for AVS (Old-Age and Survivors' Insurance), AI (Disability Insurance), and IPG (Maternity/Paternity Loss of Earnings Allowance) is 5.3% of the gross salary at the employee's expense.
The employer contributes additional amounts (5.3% AVS/AI for the employer) plus contributions for Unemployment Insurance (UI) and Family Allowance Compensation Insurance (FACI), with a total rate of 1.1% (with an annual maximum contribution limit). Accident Insurance (LAINF) ranges between 0.7% and 1.5% depending on the professional sector.
For the second pillar LPP (Professional Pension Fund), the percentages vary between 7% and 18% depending on the age group, with contributions starting from the age of 25. This multi-level structure (first pillar AVS, second pillar LPP, and the possibility of a third pillar 3a) creates a pension system significantly different from Italy.
### Permit G and Administrative Registration
The first administrative step is to obtain Permit G (Residence Permit for Cross-Border Workers), which authorizes daily commuting between your Italian residence and your workplace in Ticino. The application must be submitted to the competent Migration Office of the canton where you work, in coordination with the local Swiss authority.
Simultaneously, you must register with the Register of Foreign Residents at the competent Italian Consulate and notify the change of tax residence to the Municipality of Sumirago and the Italian Revenue Agency. These steps are crucial to avoid administrative incompatibilities between the two countries and to ensure that your tax residence in Sumirago is correctly recognized.
### Health Insurance and Coverage Choice
As a cross-border worker, you have the right to opt for Swiss health insurance (LAMal — Health Insurance Law) or maintain Italian coverage. LAMal provides deductibles for adults ranging from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500 annually, depending on the chosen insurance model.
This choice should be carefully evaluated based on the frequency of use of healthcare services and the ease of access to medical centers. If you opt for LAMal, you can access Ticino hospitals; if you remain in Italy, you can access Lombardy facilities. Health coverage represents a significant element in the monthly budget of a cross-border worker and directly influences the decision to maintain residence in Sumirago.
To evaluate the different coverage options, consult the [information on cross-border health insurance](nav:health) available on the site to compare deductibles and premiums.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ## Concrete steps for the transfer
If you decide to move your residence to Sumirago while continuing to work in Ticino, the administrative process must follow a logical sequence to avoid delays or complications.
### Essential document checklist
The required documentation includes:
1. **Residence permit/G permit**: Request from the Migration Office (SEM) of the canton where you work, usually through your employer. Required: employment contract, Italian residence documentation, and possibly health certificates.
2. Income declaration: Model 730 or Model Unico, completed with the CE section for tax credit, to be submitted in Italy with Swiss income data.
3. Registration with authorities: Notification to the Italian Consulate, the Municipality of Sumirago (change of residence), the Tax Agency (notification of cross-border activity start).
4. Opening a bank account: Many Ticino employers prefer to credit the salary to Swiss bank accounts; check if this is mandatory or optional in your case.
5. Contribution certificates: Periodic requests for INPS extracts (for the payment of coordination contributions between the two countries) and AVS certificates from Switzerland through the Federal Contributions Administration (AFC/ESTV).
### Times and administrative horizon
The request for the G permit can take from 4 to 8 weeks from the moment of complete documentation submission, depending on the canton and the competent office. Meanwhile, coordinate with your Ticino employer to synchronize the transition from Italian to Swiss taxation at the time of approval.
The income declaration must be submitted annually: in Switzerland, there is no centralized federal declaration system like in Italy (it is managed at the cantonal level), while in Italy the standard deadline is May 31 for the pre-filled 730 (extendable to September 30). Plan these annual obligations in your agenda.
### Where to find official information and support
For procedural details, rely on official channels:
- SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs): Resources on worker mobility and cross-border commuters.
- SEM (State Secretariat for Migration): Competent for G permit and cross-border residence requests.
- Tax Agency (Italy): Tax management, CE section, and tax credit.
- INPS (Italy): Verification of coordination contributions and pension management.
- AFC/ESTV (Federal Contributions Administration Switzerland): Clarifications on federal taxation and contributions.
Use these official channels before relying on unverified private consultants, especially for initial obligations.
### Estimating net monthly income
An essential step is to estimate your net monthly income, taking into account all deductions. The [paycheck calculator](nav:calculator) allows you to simulate the impact of AVS deductions (5.3%), LPP contributions, accident insurance (LAINF), and the different cantonal rates for Ticino, so you can understand how much money you actually have left compared to the agreed gross salary.
With this planning, you can evaluate whether the cost of living in Sumirago (rents, services, daily commutes to Ticino) remains compatible with the expected net income and whether the transfer represents an economically convenient choice for your situation.

item.description: Permit G, tax at source, AVS, LAMal: complete guide for border workers from Giussano (Como) working in Ticino. Taxation, time, costs.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - New border agreement in force from 1 January 2024 changes taxation and exemption - Permit G allows work in Ticino with residence in Giussano (Como) - Withholding tax withheld in Switzerland, refunds by Italian declaration - Mandatory LAMal with excess CHF 300-2500 for adults
## Key facts - **What**: Cross-border work in Giussano-Ticino with Italian/Swiss taxation - When: From 1 January 2024 (new agreement) - Where: Como (Giussano) → Ticino (Lugano, Bellinzona, Locarno) - Who: Cross-border commuters with G permit (EU/EFTA citizens) - Taxation CH: Withholding tax withheld in Switzerland - IT taxation: personal income tax with tax credit (EC framework 730) - Protection: AVS/AI/IPG 5.3% + AD/AC 1.1% + LAMal
From 1 January 2024, the new tax agreement between Italy and Switzerland has renewed the rules for those who reside in Giussano or in the municipalities of Comasco and work in Ticino. Thanks to the G (border) permit, it is possible to work regularly in the Canton of Ticino while maintaining residence in Italy, with taxation taking place mainly in Switzerland. The tax at source is withheld directly by the Ticino employer, while Italy recognizes a tax credit through the EC framework of declaration 730. This double regime, administered by the Italian-Swiss Convention of 9 December 1976, offers protection against double taxation thanks to the credit mechanism rather than exemption.
For those who choose to move to ### Taxation: How the Double System Works
The peculiarity of the cross-border worker lies in the double tax regime. In Switzerland, the employer withholds the withholding tax directly from the salary. The Swiss social contribution rates are: - AVS/AI/IPG: 5.3% (employee's share) - AD/AC: 1.1% (on income up to CHF 148,200) - LAINF: 0.7–1.5% (accident insurance) - LPP: 7–18% depending on age class (from 25 years onwards)
Approximate total: 14–25% of gross, variable by age and seniority.
In Italy, the cross-border worker is subject to IRPEF with progressive rates: 23% up to €28,000, 35% from €28,001 to €50,000, 43% over €50,000. But Italy recognizes a tax credit in the CE section of the 730 declaration, so if Switzerland has already withheld taxes, the cross-border worker does not pay a second tax. It is a credit mechanism, not an exemption: if Switzerland has withheld little, Italy completes; if it has withheld much, the cross-border worker gets a refund.
### New 2024 Agreement: Exemptions and Allowances
From January 1, 2024, the new agreement provides: - **Old cross-border workers** (already such before July 17, 2023): exemption of €7,500 of income, with transitional regime 2024–2033 - New cross-border workers: allowance of €10,000
This means that part of the income is not subject to Italian taxation, reducing the effective rate and favoring those with moderate incomes. The advantage is already evident in the income tax return of the following year, when the cross-border worker applies the allowance to the declared income.
### Social Protection: AVS, LPP and LAMal
The choice to live in Giussano while working in Ticino entails the obligation to enroll in the Swiss social systems. The AVS is the first mandatory pension pillar, guaranteed by the federal state. The LPP (professional pension) is the second pillar, provided by the employer's pension fund. The LAMal (health insurance) is mandatory, with adult deductibles ranging from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500 depending on the chosen policy. These costs are added to the gross salary but guarantee Swiss pension and health protection, often more advantageous than the Italian one for those working full-time in Ticino.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### Step 1: G Permit Application The first step is to obtain the G permit from the Ticino cantonal and municipal authorities. The application must be submitted to the Italian municipality of residence (in this case, the municipality of Giussano) or at a delegated entity's office. The following are required: - Work contract in Ticino - Italian residence certificate - Completed application form - Copy of passport/identity card The permit is valid for one or more years and must be renewed periodically at the same offices.
### Step 2: Opening a Bank Account in Ticino Many Ticino employers pay salaries directly into a CH or IT account. It is advisable to open a current account with a Ticino bank or an institution operating in the border area to easily manage CHF/EUR exchange operations and the payment of Swiss bills (rent, utilities, taxes). This also simplifies the traceability of income for tax declaration.
### Step 3: Enrollment in AVS, LPP, and LAMal Enrollment in AVS and LPP is done automatically by the employer once the contract is signed in Ticino. Communication is made to the cantonal AVS compensation fund. For LAMal (health insurance), the cross-border worker has the right to choose: they can stay in Switzerland (through a CH insurer) or remain in the Italian National Health Service with private integration. The options should be evaluated according to personal medical needs and costs.
### Step 4: Annual Italian Tax Declaration (730 or Unico) By May 31 of the following year, the cross-border worker submits the Italian tax return (model 730 or Unico) to the Revenue Agency. In the CE section, they must report income received in Switzerland, taxes withheld in Switzerland, and tax credit to avoid double taxation. The refund (if due) is usually paid within a few months.
### Step 5: Annual Documentation and Monitoring Always keep monthly/annual certificates from the Swiss employer (income statement, taxes withheld), bank statements proving salary transfers, communications from the health insurance (active coverage), and AVS statements (contribution statement). These documents are essential for the Italian declaration and for any tax checks.

item.title: Amazon leaves Malpensa: the Cub denounces ten years of precarious work
item.description: Amazon moves logistics activities from Terminal 2 in Malpensa to Brescia Montichiari, after ten years of presence. The Cub denounces the massive use of precarious contracts.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Amazon moves activities from Malpensa T2 to Brescia Montichiari. - The closure will take place next Monday after ten years of presence. - The Cub union denounces massive use of precarious contracts. - About 200 Mle workers are involved in the relocation.
## Key facts - **What**: Transfer of Amazon's logistics activities. - When: Next Monday. - Where: Malpensa Airport, Terminal 2. - Who: Mle and Cub Trasporti union. - Amount: About 200 workers affected.
The activity related to Amazon flights at Malpensa Terminal 2 is coming to a definitive end, scheduled for next Monday, following the decision to transfer logistics operations to Brescia Montichiari Airport. This move marks the end of a decade-long period during which the multinational has been a key player at the Varese airport through the company Mle, which was responsible for operational activities. The handover between the two airports urgently reopens the debate on employment dynamics in the area, focusing attention on the stability of workers in the airport logistics sector, many of whom are employed through the partner company.
### Union criticism The Cub Trasporti union has expressed a strong critical position regarding the employment conditions observed over this decade, arguing that the service has been primarily guaranteed through the use of precarious personnel and seasonal contracts. According to the union, this method has been maintained despite e-commerce becoming a structural component of the global economy, effectively depriving the activity of its real seasonal nature that would justify contractual flexibility. The union also criticizes the systematic use of fixed-term contracts, facilitated in the past by agreements signed with confederate organizations and Flai, which have allowed a significant increase in the number of temporary workers. Data provided by Cub indicates that the percentage of fixed-term contracts has reached significant levels, covering about 80% of the workforce employed in the warehouse adjacent to the entrance of Terminal 2. The union's reflection highlights a constant turnover of hundreds of workers, many of whom are not confirmed at the end of their terms or are pushed to leave their jobs due to the proposed working conditions. The analysis of the employment situation at Malpensa Terminal 2 reveals a complex picture, where the shift structure, closely linked to Amazon's flight scheduling, has imposed an extremely fragmented employment model. In addition to fixed-term contracts, Cub Trasporti reports the widespread use of various contractual types, including six-hour part-time contracts, on-call contracts, and apprenticeship placements. This mosaic of employment formulas has characterized the daily life of most workers employed by Mle. Out of a total workforce of over 750 employees, union data indicates the presence of over 200 precarious workers, with a significant concentration in the activities of Terminal 2, where approximately 180 workers are employed on fixed-term contracts out of a total of nearly 200 people.

The dispute involving Mle workers has also reached the institutional table of the Lombardy Region. It is necessary to underline that, during the first meeting dedicated to the specific situation of Amazon, Cub Trasporti, together with other grassroots organizations, did not participate. Cub's assessment of the outcome of the confrontation between the confederate unions, Uil, and the company remains negative: the union maintains that no concrete commitment has emerged from the companies to ensure lasting stability for all workers involved. While the confederate organizations have expressed moderate optimism about the relocation opportunities offered by Mle, Cub insists on the need for a more active and decisive role from the institutions in the face of the decisions of multinationals. For workers who are in a phase of contractual transition, the recommended procedure involves constant monitoring of the agreements signed between the social parties and the company. ## In brief - Cut of 2,174 school staff nationwide. - In Lombardy, 205 fewer positions are expected for the 2026/2027 school year. - The measure stems from Law 207 of December 30, 2024. - Unions such as CGIL and UIL contest the government's decision.
- **What**: Reduction of school staff (ATA). - When: 2026/2027 school year. - Where: Italy and Lombardy region. - Who: Ministry of Education and unions (CGIL, UIL). - Amount: 205 fewer positions in Lombardy, 2,174 in Italy. - Legislation: Law 207 of December 30, 2024 (2025 Budget Law).
The 2026/2027 school year opens with a significant reduction in the staff of ATA personnel, particularly school staff. Official tables confirm a national reduction that brings the available positions from 131,143 to 128,969 units, marking a decrease of 2,174 positions. In this scenario, Lombardy suffers a reduction of 205 units, going from 19,736 to 19,531 staff. This measure is legally based on Law 207 of December 30, 2024, known as the 2025 Budget Law, which in Article 1, paragraph 828, provided for the cut plan starting from the current school year. The subsequent implementation occurred through Ministerial Decree 211 of November 2025, concentrating the cuts mainly on secondary schools. Trade union organizations, particularly FLC CGIL and UIL Scuola, have expressed strong opposition to these provisions, emphasizing that the numerical reduction cannot disregard the real needs of school buildings. The main concern is the ability of schools to maintain adequate standards of supervision and assistance.
### The union position The FLC CGIL Lombardy union had already raised the issue last May, highlighting that the cuts affect regional high schools. For the union, it is not just a matter of statistical calculations but a direct threat to the quality of the educational offer. The presence of school staff is considered essential for the daily management of common spaces, laboratories, and gyms, as well as for ensuring the safety of students. UIL Scuola reiterated its opposition to the measure, warning that the staff reduction risks compromising the functionality of the institutions. Despite assurances, the fear is that the reduction in staff may have negative repercussions on cleaning and supervision, fundamental elements for the regular conduct of lessons in a safe and well-managed environment. The analysis of the criteria used to define the 2026/27 staffing levels shows how the Government has based its choices on the prediction of demographic decline and school population, introducing a specific corrective for the presence of students with disabilities. At the national level, the ATA staffing has been set at 194,303 units. However, the point of friction between institutions and unions lies precisely in this calculation methodology. The union representatives argue that the decrease in the number of students does not automatically lead to a reduction in the workload for ATA staff. Maintenance, supervision, and assistance must be guaranteed regardless of demographic fluctuations, as the physical structures — corridors, bathrooms, gyms, and laboratories — remain the same. This discrepancy between bureaucratic parameters and daily operational needs creates growing tension within the Lombardy school system.

item.title: Living in Daverio, working in Ticino as a border worker
item.description: Complete guide for Italian border workers: G permit, source tax, double taxation, AVS, LPP and how to maximize your salary working in Switzerland.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Frontaliero = withholding tax ONLY in Switzerland; Italy avoids double taxation with tax credit (CE 730 form) - New Frontalier Agreement in effect from January 1, 2024: exemption €7,500 (old frontalieri), €10,000 (new) - Permit G is the essential document for working in Switzerland as a foreign resident
## Key facts - **What**: Frontaliero = worker residing in Italy, employed in Switzerland with permit G - When: New Agreement from January 1, 2024; Italo-Swiss Convention from December 9, 1976 - Where: Daverio (Varese, Italy) → Ticino (Switzerland) - Who: SECO, Canton Ticino, Tax Agency, AFC/ESTV - Exemption: €7,500 (old frontalieri), €10,000 (new); transitional regime 2024-2033 - Permit: Permit G for foreign resident frontalieri - Taxes: Withholding tax ONLY in Switzerland; tax credit in Italy (CE 730 form)
Daverio, a municipality in the province of Varese a few kilometers from the Ticino border, is an increasingly popular choice for those who decide to work in Switzerland while maintaining residency in Italy. The geographical position, the lower cost of living compared to Ticino, and the tax benefits of the New Frontalier Agreement signed on December 23, 2020 (in effect from January 1, 2024) make this option attractive to thousands of commuters.
The tax regime for frontalieri who live in Daverio and work in Ticino is based on two normative pillars: the Convention to avoid double taxation between Italy and Switzerland (December 9, 1976) and the New Frontalier Agreement (in effect from January 1, 2024 with Law 83 of June 13, 2023 in Italy). This framework ensures that the withholding tax is deducted ONLY in Switzerland by the employer, while Italy avoids double taxation by recognizing a tax credit in the CE section of the income tax return (model 730).
A frontaliero who resides in Daverio and works for a Ticino company does not pay the same taxes twice: they pay taxes in Switzerland (withholding tax, AVS, LPP, LAMal) and then declare the income in Italy, obtaining a tax credit from the Italian tax authorities corresponding to the taxes already paid in Switzerland. If the Swiss taxes are higher than the Italian ones—which is the case in most situations—the frontaliero benefits from a net refund.
### Permit G: the essential document
Permit G (frontaliero permit) is the document that authorizes an Italian citizen residing in Daverio to work in Switzerland. It is a document tied to Switzerland (not transferable to other countries), renewed annually or for multi-year cycles, and administered by the Canton Ticino and the federal authorities SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs).
Anyone who resides permanently in Daverio and signs a work contract with a Ticino company must submit the application for Permit G to the competent cantonal office in Ticino. The request is processed in coordination with the Swiss employer and the Italian authorities (to verify the continuity of residence). Not all contracts are eligible: the employer must demonstrate that the job cannot be filled by Swiss citizens, EU/AELS members, or other frontalieri already present in the market.
Once the Permit G is obtained, the frontaliero from Daverio enters the special tax regime of the New Agreement. Old frontalieri (those who were frontalieri before July 17, 2023) benefit from an annual exemption of €7,500 on employment income, with a transitional regime until 2033. New frontalieri benefit from an annual exemption of €10,000. These thresholds mean that part of the income declared in Italy is not subject to Italian taxation, reducing the overall tax burden. ### Double taxation and tax credit: how it really works
A cross-border worker living in Daverio and earning CHF 60,000 gross per year is subject to Swiss withholding tax (withholding tax) directly from their paycheck by their Ticino employer. The rate varies depending on the canton, the Ticino municipality of work, and the income, but it averages between 10% and 18% of the gross amount.
Simultaneously, the cross-border worker is obliged to declare their Swiss income in Italy to the Revenue Agency. The declared income is taxed according to the Italian IRPEF rates: 23% up to €28,000, 35% from €28,001 to €50,000, 43% over €50,000. However, by applying the tax credit for taxes paid in Switzerland (CE section of the 730 form), this credit fully or partially compensates for the Italian taxation, avoiding the payment of the same taxes twice.
To illustrate: a cross-border worker earns CHF 50,000 gross. The Swiss withholding tax is approximately CHF 7,500. The income is declared in Italy as the equivalent in euros. The Italian IRPEF would result in approximately €3,000. The tax credit recognizes the CHF 7,500 already paid in Switzerland, zeroing or almost zeroing the Italian tax due. The exemption of €7,500 (old cross-border workers) or €10,000 (new) further reduces the Italian taxable amount.
### Social contributions: AVS, LPP, and health insurance
As an employee in Switzerland, the cross-border worker automatically pays contributions for old-age insurance (AVS), disability insurance (AI), and unemployment insurance (IPG) as an employee, totaling 5.3% of the gross salary. An additional 1.1% goes to accident insurance (AD/AC), with a cap of CHF 148,200 annual income. The temporary insolvency insurance (LAINF) costs between 0.7% and 1.5%.
For professional pension (LPP, second pillar), the employee's contribution varies from 7% to 18% depending on age (from 25 years onwards) and the employer. These payments build an additional pension to the basic AVS pension, essential for maintaining the standard of living after retirement.
Health insurance (LAMal) is mandatory in Switzerland. Cross-border workers with a G permit have the right to choose: they can insure with a Swiss health insurance company (deductibles from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500 annually for adults) or, in some cases, maintain enrollment in the Italian National Health Service if the cantonal legislation allows it. The choice has implications for health coverage and overall costs.
### Italian taxation on foreign income
Italy taxes Italian residents on all income, regardless of where it is generated (worldwide taxation principle). However, the Italian-Swiss Convention and the New Cross-Border Agreement allow for the reduction or elimination of double taxation. The cross-border worker must complete the income tax return (730 form or Redditi PF) by entering the Swiss income in the CE section (foreign income) and indicating the taxes paid in Switzerland. The Revenue Agency calculates the tax credit (ordinary credit) and applies it directly to the Italian tax due. If the Swiss taxes exceed the Italian ones, the cross-border worker receives a refund from the Italian tax authorities.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). Before moving to Daverio to work in Ticino, it is essential to complete a series of administrative and financial steps.

item.title: Living in Arosio, working in Ticino: border guide
item.description: From geographical location to tax advantages: everything that those who want to move to Arosio and work in the Canton of Ticino need to know about the rights of the border worker.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Arosio is on the border with Ticino: ideal location for commuters working in Switzerland - From January 1, 2024, the New Cross-Border Agreement introduces allowances of CHF 10,000 (new commuters) - Withholding tax is deducted in Switzerland; Italy avoids double taxation through tax credit - AVS/AI/IPG contributions: 5.3% borne by the employee, managed by the Ticino employer
## Key facts - **What**: Residence in Italy (Como province), work in Canton Ticino with permit G - When: Regime active from January 1, 2024 for all new commuters - Where: Arosio (Como, Italy) — border crossings to Ticino (Chiasso, Brogeda, Gaggiolo) - Who: Commuters with permit G, administered by Swiss SEM and Italian Revenue Agency - Allowance amount: CHF 10,000 annually (new commuters); CHF 7,500 (previous commuters, transitional regime 2024–2033) - Withholding tax rate: Set by federal regulations and cantonal tax administrations
### Arosio: a logical choice for commuters Arosio is a municipality in the province of Como, located a few kilometers from the Swiss border. Its proximity to the crossings connecting Lombardy to Ticino (Chiasso, Brogeda, Gaggiolo) makes it a convenient residential base for those working in major Ticino centers: Lugano, Mendrisio, Bellinzona, Locarno. The cost of living in the Como area is generally lower compared to the Canton of Ticino, a non-secondary element for commuters who receive Swiss salaries but support part of their personal life in Italy. The local community offers healthcare, educational, and administrative services, with the Como Revenue Agency available for Italian tax issues. The geographical proximity reduces commuting times, a crucial factor for those who face border crossings daily. For a commuter, choosing to reside in Arosio means balancing access to the Ticino job market with the economic sustainability of Italian residence. ### The tax regime of the cross-border worker: how it works
Anyone residing in Arosio and working in Ticino is subject to the G permit (cross-border), which allows daily or weekly commuting. From a tax perspective, the withholding tax (deducted by the Swiss employer) is paid exclusively in Switzerland — never in both countries. This is a fundamental principle: the income from dependent work of a cross-border worker is never taxed twice. Italy, through the Italo-Swiss Bilateral Convention signed on December 9, 1976, grants a tax credit (section CE of the 730 declaration) that compensates for the tax already paid in Switzerland. Switzerland is not a member of the EU, so taxation follows specific regimes, not the ordinary European system. The Italian tax credit is the key tool to avoid double taxation.
### Allowances and new 2024 agreement
The New Cross-Border Agreement, signed on December 23, 2020, and effective from January 1, 2024, has redefined the tax allowances. For new cross-border workers (those not yet registered as such before July 17, 2023), the allowance is CHF 10,000 annually: incomes up to this threshold do not generate income tax in Ticino. Cross-border workers already active before July 17, 2023, benefit from a transitional regime: an allowance of CHF 7,500 from 2024 to 2033, with gradual increases up to CHF 10,000. This distinction is important for correctly calculating the taxable base and planning the income declaration. The Italian Revenue Agency recognizes the tax credit in section CE, reducing or zeroing the gross Italian IRPEF according to the ordinary rates: 23% up to 28,000 euros, 35% up to 50,000, 43% over 50,000.
### Pension contributions: AVS, LPP, and health insurance
Cross-border workers pay Swiss social security contributions: AVS (Old-Age and Survivors' Insurance) and AI (Disability Insurance) at a rate of 5.3% of the gross salary at the employee's expense, plus an equivalent employer contribution. The IPG (Loss of Earnings Allowance) contribution of 0.3% is added. Unemployment insurance (AD) and accident insurance (LAINF) follow federal rates: respectively 1.1% up to CHF 148,200 annual salary and 0.7-1.5%. The LPP (occupational pension, second pillar) varies by age group: from 7% to 18% depending on the pension fund and professional category. In Italy, the equivalent is managed by INPS (National Institute for Social Security), but a cross-border worker working in Switzerland pays exclusively Swiss contributions: they do not pay simultaneously in both systems. Health insurance (LAMal) is mandatory in Switzerland; cross-border workers with a G permit have the right to choose and can insure themselves with a Swiss institution or maintain Italian coverage (with verification of regulatory compatibility). The deductibles for adults in LAMal range from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### Practical procedure: what to do before moving
#### 1. Request the G permit
Before moving to Arosio, the Ticino employer must submit a request for authorization to hire to the SEM (Swiss State Secretariat for Migration) and the competent cantonal authorities. The G permit is nominative (linked to the employer) and has a maximum validity of 5 years, renewable. The documentation requires: signed employment contract, curriculum vitae, Swiss employer identification, proof of minimum income (determined at the cantonal level). It is advisable to verify the specific details with the Como Prefecture (Italian side) and the Department of Finance and Economy of the Canton Ticino (Swiss side).
#### 2. Open a bank account and Italian tax formalities
On the Italian side, it is necessary to register with the competent Agenzia Entrate for the province of Como (office of Arosio or district) and obtain or update the tax code. Those who work in Switzerland must inform the Municipality of Arosio that they are cross-border workers: this communication facilitates the recognition of status with the local public administration. A bank account with an Italian bank in Como or Switzerland is essential: many Ticino employers pay salaries via SEPA bank transfer, so it is useful to have an Italian or Swiss IBAN. Some cross-border workers open accounts with banks operating in Switzerland, simplifying administrative management.
#### 3. Income declaration and CE section
Every year (by June 30 for the ordinary declaration), those who work in Ticino must submit the 730 model to the Agenzia Entrate of the province of Como. In the 730 model, the **CE section** is specific for cross-border workers: here, the tax already paid in Switzerland (withheld by the employer) is declared and the tax credit is quantified. The Agenzia Entrate compares the Italian tax due (gross IRPEF according to ordinary rates) with the recognized credit and determines the refund, the integration, or the balance due. It is advisable to use a tax accountant specialized in cross-border taxation to ensure the correct compilation of the CE section and maximize the credit.
#### 4. Key contacts and resources
For Swiss tax issues: Canton Ticino, Division of Contributions (federal section); for work permit: SEM (Canton Ticino section). For Italian aspects: Agenzia Entrate Como (district office), Municipality of Arosio (secretariat/registry), Como Prefecture (general administrative issues). A net salary calculator is available on our website to estimate the impact of taxes and contributions on the Swiss paycheck before the decision to move.
#### Critical deadlines
- G permit request: To be submitted before the official start date of work (usually 2-4 weeks in advance) - Agenzia Entrate registration: Within 30 days of starting Italian residence - 730 declaration: By June 30 of the year following the income received - AVS contribution payment: Monthly or on the schedule indicated by the employer (usually at the end of the month)
Moving to Arosio as a cross-border worker is administratively feasible if planned in advance. The interaction between Swiss and Italian rules requires attention to detail and respect for deadlines. To avoid surprises from the paycheck or tax declaration, use our net salary calculator and verify in advance the impact of Swiss-Italian taxation on your income. Then, contact the competent administrations or a specialized consultant to further refine the contractual and pension details.

item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Operational protocol between Niguarda Hospital and the National Cancer Institute of Milan - Objective: to avoid interruptions in the care pathway of cancer patients - Coordination by ATS Milan and the University of Milan
## Key facts - **What**: Operational protocol between Niguarda Hospital and the National Cancer Institute - When: Not specified - Where: Milan - Who: Niguarda Hospital, National Cancer Institute, ATS Milan, University of Milan - Amount: Not specified
Niguarda Hospital and the Fondazione IRCCS National Cancer Institute (INT) of Milan have signed an operational protocol to ensure continuity of care for cancer patients in case of emergencies. The protocol, coordinated by ATS of the Metropolitan City of Milan and the School of Medical Oncology of the University of Milan, aims to avoid interruptions in the care pathway of patients. The National Cancer Institute, a reference center for cancer care and research, does not have its own Emergency Department, so patients who face an emergency may need to access another hospital facility.
### Protocol Objective The protocol aims to ensure that the transition from one institution to another occurs without interrupting the continuity of care, by putting the emergency department of Niguarda in direct communication with the specialists of the INT. When a patient being treated at the National Cancer Institute arrives at the Niguarda Emergency Department, emergency professionals can promptly coordinate with the oncologists of the INT, sharing clinical information, ongoing therapies, and care priorities. The goal is to allow Niguarda doctors to intervene while considering the oncological pathway already undertaken by the patient.
The primary objective remains to stabilize the person and address the emergency, but the connection between the teams also serves to avoid inappropriate interventions and, when conditions allow, to facilitate the patient's return to their reference oncology center. According to the protocol, in most cases, the resumption of care by the National Cancer Institute occurs within 24-48 hours of the Emergency Department notification.
Even when immediate transfer is not possible, the exchange between specialists allows for continuity in clinical decisions and therapy management. The project fits into the model of clinical-assistance networks promoted by the Lombardy Region, with the aim of strengthening collaboration between facilities and professionals and reducing the fragmentation of care pathways.
In this case, the Lombardy Oncological Network and the emergency-urgency system are connected, creating a structured link between a reference oncology institute and a large Emergency Department. ### Implications for Cross-Border Workers The operational protocol between Niguarda Hospital and the National Cancer Institute of Milan has important implications for cross-border workers who work in Lombardy and reside in Ticino. This agreement ensures that cross-border cancer patients can receive continuous and coordinated care in case of emergencies, avoiding interruptions in their treatment path.
### Procedure for Cross-Border Patients When a cross-border patient undergoing treatment at the National Cancer Institute arrives at the Niguarda Emergency Department, emergency professionals can promptly coordinate with the oncologists at the INT, sharing clinical information, ongoing therapies, and care priorities. This allows Niguarda doctors to intervene while considering the oncological path already undertaken by the patient.
### Possible Scenarios A cross-border worker in a similar situation could benefit from this protocol, ensuring that their therapies are not interrupted and that they continue to receive appropriate care. The protocol provides that in most cases, the resumption of care by the National Cancer Institute will occur within 24-48 hours of the Emergency Department notification.
### Actions for Cross-Border Workers Cross-border workers facing a medical emergency can rely on this protocol to ensure the continuity of their care. It is important that patients and their families are informed about this procedure and that they promptly turn to the Niguarda Emergency Department in case of emergency.
### Deadlines and Procedure The operational protocol is already in effect, and patients can immediately benefit from this collaboration between the two facilities. There are no specific deadlines to be met, but it is crucial that patients follow the doctors' instructions and present themselves at the Niguarda Emergency Department if needed.

Additionally, the [tax calculator](nav:calculator) can be used to obtain detailed information about their tax and insurance situation.

Cross-border workers who work in Lombardy and reside in Ticino can benefit from this initiative, which ensures them coordinated and timely assistance in case of need.

Living in Griante and working in Canton Ticino as a cross-border worker is a common choice for those seeking a balance between living space, quality of life, and job opportunities. From 1 January 2024, with the new cross-border agreement (Law 83 of 13 June 2023, signed on 23 December 2020), the rules for taxation and social security are clearly defined and ensure legal clarity.
The cross-border worker "G" is legally defined as a person residing abroad who works in Switzerland, commuting daily or at least once a week. For Italians, the tax regime is particularly advantageous: the withholding tax on employment income is deducted exclusively by Switzerland, not by Italy. The convention against double taxation of 9 December 1976 guarantees this mechanism; in the Italian declaration (CE section of the 730 form), a tax credit is applied for the amount already paid in Switzerland.
### Social security contributions and pay structure
Those working in Switzerland must contribute to various social security schemes: AVS (first pillar) at 5.3% for the employee, plus an additional 5.3% from the employer; AI (disability insurance) and IPG (maternity allowance) included in the 5.3%; LPP (second pillar, company pension fund) from 7% to 18% depending on age, starting at 25 years; AD and AC (unemployment and insolvency) at 1.1% with a cap at CHF 148.200; LAINF (occupational accidents) between 0.7% and 1.5%. These contributions are managed at the federal level by the AFC (Federal Tax Administration). The AVS contributions paid in Switzerland are recognized by the Italian INPS for the right to the Italian pension.
### Health insurance and LAMal
As a cross-border worker, you have the option to choose health insurance: you can maintain Italian coverage or join a Swiss health insurance (LAMal). The adult deductibles in LAMal range from CHF 300 to CHF 2.500 depending on the chosen insurance. Many cross-border workers opt for LAMal due to the geographical proximity to their workplace in Ticino.

Withholdings for AVS/AI/IPG (5.3%), AD/AC (1.1%), LPP (7-18%) and LAINF (0.7-1.5%) will appear in the Swiss paycheck of a border crossing. The cantonal source tax varies according to salary bracket and personal circumstances; it is calculated by the cantonal tax administrations and paid independently to the Swiss tax authorities by the employer.
In the Italian declaration, the income from foreign work must be indicated in the EC framework of form 730. The Swiss tax paid generates a tax credit that reduces or eliminates the Italian IRPEF (23% up to EUR 28,000, 35% between EUR 28,001 and EUR 50,000, 43% over EUR 50,000). For old frontier workers (before 17 July 2023) there is an exemption of CHF 7,500 on a transitional basis until 2033; new frontier workers benefit from an exemption of CHF 10,000. item.content:encoded:
## In brief
- Withholding tax only deducted in Switzerland for cross-border workers - New Cross-Border Agreement effective from 1 January 2024 - AVS/AI contributions: 5.3% for employees, LAINF 0.7–1.5% - LAMal: deductible CHF 300–2500, option right Permit G
## Key facts
- **Withholding tax**: Deducted only in Switzerland - New Agreement: Effective from 1 January 2024 - AVS/AI: 5.3% for employees - LAINF: 0.7–1.5% depending on sector - LPP: 7–18% by age group (from 25 years) - Deductible: €7,500 for old cross-border workers (until 2033), €10,000 for new ones
Bellagio, overlooking Lake Como, is a popular residential choice for those working in Ticino. The province of Como is within manageable distances from major Ticino work centers: Lugano, Mendrisio, Chiasso, Bellinzona. For this move, understanding the tax, contribution, and insurance regime governing Swiss-Italian cross-border workers is essential, especially after the New Cross-Border Agreement came into effect on 1 January 2024.
The tax system is the central pillar. The withholding tax on employment income is deducted solely by Switzerland, avoiding double taxation. Italy subsequently applies the tax credit (CE box of the 730 tax return) to recognize what has been paid to the Swiss tax authorities. This mechanism, regulated by the Convention on Double Taxation between Italy and Switzerland signed on 9 December 1976, protects the cross-border worker from excessive tax pressure.
### The tax regime: old and new cross-border workers
The New Agreement introduces a significant distinction. Old cross-border workers (those already in this status before 17 July 2023) enjoy an annual exemption of €7,500 until 2033, under a transitional regime. New cross-border workers benefit from an annual deductible of €10,000. This difference is central to the calculation of taxable income in Italy.
Swiss social security contributions are deducted directly by the Ticino company from the gross salary. The AVS/AI/IPG rate is fixed at 5.3% for employees, while the employer contributes the same amount. The accident insurance (LAINF) varies between 0.7% and 1.5%, depending on the sector. The professional pension fund (LPP) requires contributions between 7% and 18%, depending on the age group (from 25 years onwards).
The cantonal and communal tax in Ticino is added according to federal and cantonal rates, administered by the Swiss authorities. You can [calculate your net income using our tax calculator](nav:calculator) to verify exactly how much you will earn after deductions. ## What to Consider Before Moving to Bellagio
Moving to Bellagio to work in Ticino involves significant practical and financial considerations. The cost of living is the first evaluation: Bellagio is an expensive residential area on Lake Como. Rents and property prices reflect the scenic value and proximity to the Swiss border. A commuter must assess whether the net salary in Ticino (after AVS deductions of 5.3% and LAINF 0.7–1.5%) compensates for housing and commuting costs. A comparative table between monthly net income and rental costs is essential for making an informed decision.
### Advantages and Disadvantages of the Choice
The advantages of living in Bellagio include quality of life, a lakeside landscape, an established community of commuters (offering support networks and practical knowledge), and geographical proximity to Ticino, ideal for daily commuting. The disadvantages include significant rental and property costs, daily commuting on mountain roads exposed to weather variability, and the obligation to subscribe to health insurance.
Regarding the choice of insurance: commuters with Permit G have the option to choose between Swiss LAMal and Italian SSN. If you opt for LAMal, the deductibles for adults range from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500 annually, depending on the coverage. If you remain in the Italian SSN, you must notify the Swiss authorities of your renunciation of LAMal. This choice directly impacts health coverage and annual costs.
### Registration Procedure and Permit G
Before moving, ensure you have the [Permit G (commuters)](nav:permits). This is mandatory for daily work in Switzerland. The documentation is submitted by the Ticino employer, who coordinates with the Swiss authorities (SEM — State Secretariat for Migration). Without Permit G, the move is legally prohibited.
A commuter should also consider: the distance to the nearest border crossings (Brogeda, Gaggiolo, Ponte Tresa, Chiasso) closest to the workplace, the stability of the Ticino job (commuting jobs are more affected by economic conditions), and the effect of currency (salary in CHF, expenses in EUR, with exchange rate fluctuations impacting purchasing power).
### Opportunity Cost Calculation
Before any move, subtract fixed costs from the gross monthly amount: AVS/AI/IPG 5.3%, LAINF 0.7–1.5%, LPP 7–18%, federal and cantonal Ticino withholding tax. Compare the resulting net amount with rents, utilities, commuting costs (fuel, maintenance, or public transport subscriptions), and living expenses in Bellagio. If the margin is positive and sustainable over time, the move is economically justified.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ## Checklist for moving and starting as a cross-border commuter
Step 1: Calculate your net monthly income
Before any move, estimate your net income using a [cross-border tax calculator](nav:calculator). Subtract from the gross amount: - AVS/AI/IPG: 5.3% - LAINF: between 0.7% and 1.5% (depends on the sector) - LPP: between 7% and 18% (depends on age, from 25 onwards) - Federal and cantonal Ticino withholding tax
The result is your net monthly income, to be compared with the actual cost of rent, utilities, and living in Bellagio.
Step 2: Verify the G Permit with your employer
Ensure you obtain the G Permit before moving. The Ticino employer submits the documentation to the Swiss authorities (SEM). This permit is mandatory for daily work in Switzerland and is not a formality you can handle independently: your employer coordinates the process.
Step 3: Choose health insurance (LAMal or Italian SSN)
With the G Permit, you have the option to: - Join the Swiss LAMal (deductible CHF 300–2.500 for adults, depending on the chosen coverage) - Stay in the Italian SSN (with official notification to the Swiss authorities)
The choice affects premiums/deductibles and coverage. Consult a LAMal agent or local health authorities to evaluate which solution is best.
Step 4: Italian tax registration and communication to the Revenue Agency
Notify the Italian Revenue Agency of the change of residence. Your income will be subject to the new cross-border regime: - If you are an old cross-border commuter (already such before July 17, 2023): exemption €7.500 annually until 2033 - If you are a new cross-border commuter: exemption €10.000 annually
These exemptions reduce the Italian taxable income and result in lower tax payments.
Step 5: Swiss bank account and currency management
Many cross-border commuters maintain accounts in both countries to manage CHF (salary) and EUR (expenses). Open an account with a Ticino bank. Check exchange fees and management costs: some institutions offer cross-border accounts with advantageous conditions.
Step 6: Calculate the total cost of commuting and decide on the means
Estimate fuel (if private car), travel (if train/bus), vehicle maintenance, Swiss vignette if necessary. Some cross-border commuters choose public transport (Trenitalia + Swiss railways) to avoid the costs and stress of daily driving. Compare all options with the gross salary advantage: if the commuting cost is too high, the move might not be convenient.

item.title: Figino Serenza: guide for border workers in Ticino
item.description: Permit G, taxation, LAMal and costs: everything that changes if you live in Figino Serenza and work in the Canton of Ticino as a border worker.
item.content:encoded:
## In short - Permit G mandatory to work in Ticino from Lombardy - Withholding tax only in Switzerland, no double taxation - LAMal mandatory in Switzerland with CHF 300–2500 deductibles - AVS/LPP: contributions 5.3% on salary + employer payments
## Key facts - **What**: Permit G + taxation for cross-border workers - When: From January 1, 2024 (new agreement in force) - Where: Cross-border workers Italy-Ticino from Lombardy - Who: SEM, SECO, Tax Agency, INPS - Tax rate: Single in Switzerland, tax credit in Italy - LAMal deductible: CHF 300–2500 annual for adults - Tax exemption threshold: €7,500 (historic from 17/7/2023), €10,000 (new cross-border workers)
Those who choose to live in Figino Serenza and work in the Canton of Ticino have access to an increasingly common opportunity among cross-border workers: staying in Lombardy, maintaining Italian residency, but transferring the Swiss salary. However, this model involves precise rules for taxation, social security, and insurance. The Permit G (authorization from the SEM) is the first mandatory document.
### Permit G and Tax Treatment
The Permit G allows Italian residents to work legally in Switzerland. Those living in Figino Serenza must apply for it at the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) at least 6–8 weeks before the start date of work. Required documents: signed job offer, passport or ID card, residence certificate from the Italian municipality, proof of LAMal subscription.
A key point: the withholding tax is deducted exclusively in Switzerland. There is no double taxation CHF-EUR. The Convention between Italy and Switzerland of December 9, 1976 regulates this matter. Italy does not tax income from work carried out in Switzerland for cross-border workers; rather, they declare the income in the Italian model 730 and apply the tax credit (CE section) to avoid overlaps.
The New Cross-Border Workers Agreement, signed on December 23, 2020 and entered into force on January 1, 2024 (Law 83 of June 13, 2023 in Italy), introduces tax-free thresholds: historic cross-border workers (those already such before July 17, 2023) enjoy an exemption up to €7,500 annually in a transitional regime until 2033; new cross-border workers have a threshold of €10,000.
### LAMal and Social Security
Swiss health insurance (LAMal) is mandatory for all workers. The cross-border worker must subscribe to it within 3 months of the start of the employment relationship. Deductibles for adults range from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500 annually, depending on the policy and chosen fund. The employer typically covers a portion of the premium according to the collective agreement.
On the social security front, AVS/AI/IPG contributions (employee part) are 5.3% of gross salary. The company pays the same 5.3%. For unemployment (AD/AC), the rate is 1.1% with a cap of CHF 148,200 on annual salary. Accident insurance (LAINF) varies between 0.7% and 1.5% depending on the sector. The second pillar (LPP, supplementary pension) involves contributions between 7% and 18% depending on age, from the 25th year of age. Living in Lombardy, Working in Switzerland: The Economic Calculation
One of the main advantages of living in Figino Serenza and working in Ticino is the cost of living differential. Housing, food, and services in Lombardy are generally lower than in Ticino. This allows for a significant monthly savings potential. However, the commuter must balance this benefit with the recurring costs of commuting: fuel, highway A2 (for which the annual Swiss vignette CHF 40 is required), parking at the Ticino workplace, possible tolls.
The salary is paid in CHF (Swiss francs), while housing, food, and local expenses in Figino Serenza are in EUR (euros). The margin of convenience depends on a careful evaluation of individual items: rent, utilities, food, transportation, healthcare services. Many commuters use [specialized salary calculators](nav:calculator) to simulate the actual net income and compare it with the cost of living.
### Border Crossings and Commuter Routes
From Figino Serenza, the commuter has access to multiple border crossings into Ticino. **Chiasso** (via highway A2) is the most direct route to southern Ticino (Lugano, Mendrisio, south of Lugano border). Brogeda is a less congested alternative during peak hours. Gaggiolo is suitable for those working in the northern lake area (Luino, areas near Ticino). Ponte Tresa serves western Sopraceneri (Locarno, Ascona, Bellinzona).
Wait times at the border vary depending on the time of day and seasonal congestion. During morning and evening peak hours, Chiasso can experience delays. Some commuters adjust their departure times or use public transportation: Como–Chiasso regional trains, then Swiss rail connection to the destination (Lugano, Bellinzona, Locarno).
Consulting [border crossing and historical traffic information](nav:traffic-history) before planning the route is a common practice.
### Administrative Issues Before Moving
Before moving from Figino Serenza to Ticino, specific bureaucratic steps must be completed:
- Notify the Figino Serenza municipality of the change of residence and obtain the residence certificate - Inform the Italian Revenue Agency of the new address and Swiss income source - Apply for a G permit with the competent SEM (State Secretariat for Migration) - Sign a LAMal contract with a Swiss insurance company (CSS, Helsana, Visana, SWICA, etc.) - Notify the Ticino company of the new address and start date - Consider opening a Swiss bank account for salary receipt (including CHF-EUR exchange fees in the evaluation) - In the first year, consult a tax advisor for correct income tax filing (CE box for tax credit)
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Step-by-Step: Transfer and First Deadlines
Step 1 — Job Search and Written Offer. Identify the Ticino company and obtain a signed and dated job offer. This document is mandatory for the G Permit application.
Step 2 — G Permit Application. Contact the competent SEM (for Ticino: SEM Bellinzona) at least 6–8 weeks before the start date. Required: passport/identity card, job offer, Italian residence certificate, proof of LAMal subscription (even provisional).
Step 3 — Change Italian Residence. Go to the Figino Serenza Town Hall and register the transfer. Obtain the residence certificate for the G Permit application and for communications with the Tax Agency.
**Step 4 — LAMal Subscription.** Contact a Swiss insurer directly and activate the coverage. Major insurance companies operate online. Note: It is mandatory within 3 months from the start of work, but it is advisable to activate it earlier for the G Permit.
Step 5 — Bank Account. Consider opening a Swiss account with UBS, Credit Suisse, Raiffeisen, or others, or receiving the salary on an Italian account with subsequent CHF-EUR exchange. Evaluate fees and spreads.
Step 6 — First Year Tax Declaration. Consult a tax advisor for the Italian 730 form. Indicate the income declared in Switzerland and the tax credit in the CE section to avoid double taxation.
### Recurring Costs to Budget
Once transferred to Figino Serenza, the cross-border worker incurs:
- Rent/mortgage: Variable depending on the area and square meters in Figino Serenza - Highway and fuel: Estimated travel (e.g., 25 km × days/week × 52 weeks), considering gasoline and vignette CHF 40/year - LAMal: CHF 300–500 monthly depending on the deductible and policy - Bank Account: If Swiss, check monthly or annual fees (some accounts offer free management if the salary is domiciled) - Currency Exchange: If salary transfer in CHF → Italian account in EUR, consider bank spreads (0.5–2% depending on the bank) - Public Transport: Possible LC (Lugano–Como) or regional train subscription if choosing a combination of car/train
### Available Tools
To simulate your net paycheck considering taxation, AVS, LAMal, and other cross-border contributions, consult [the specialized salary calculator](nav:calculator). You can enter the Swiss gross and see the actual net.
If you want to compare the cost of living in Ticino vs. bordering Lombardy (rents, goods, services), try [the cost of living comparator](nav:cost-of-living). This will help you evaluate the real savings by living in Figino Serenza.
For managing recurring CHF-EUR exchange (e.g., monthly transfers to Italian accounts), the exchange rate tool shows the best current banking conditions.
Finally, receive monthly updates on cross-border regulations, tax deadlines, and job opportunities in Ticino by subscribing to the Frontaliere Ticino newsletter — access from the [calculator section](nav:calculator).
